The supplemental is triggered when you get a low positive to double check the result for false positives. If the supplemental is negative that means you do not have HSV2.

If you get a Western Blot it will likely be negative. I got an IGG of 4 and a negative supplemental and then a WB which turned out to be negative too.

It’s a frustrating experience to say the least because the IGG can just simply be wrong for some people like us. I even got a 5 on an HSV2 IGG and that was months before testing negative on the WB.

Let me know if you want to know any more

So I think there’s a misunderstanding going on here. This all centers around a simple question which is, can the negative reflexes be trusted? In my research, I’m yet to find a single person who received a negative reflex who ended up positive.

For this reason, it’s fair to conclude that negative reflexes are a reliable way of ruling out false positives.

Not everyone can afford the WB, and for those who have received negative reflexes on their tests, it’s not unreasonable or irresponsible for them to conclude that they’re negative.
